newsitem.title: MEXICO: Modelo shares fall on Anheuser-Busch news.
newsitem.headline: Modelo shares fall on Anheuser-Busch news.

text.p: Shares of Grupo Modelo SA weakened on Wednesday following news Anheuser-Busch Cos had exercised options to increase its stake in the Mexican brewer to 37 percent for an investment of about $550 million.

Some analysts said Modelo's share price fell because Anheuser-Busch paid a strike price much below the market price for the shares, which closed off 2.25 pesos to 43.20 pesos on the Mexican Bolsa on Wednesday. The strike price had been agreed through a previously-set formula.
Anheuser-Busch bought a 17.7 percent direct stake in Modelo, Mexico's top brewer, in 1993 for $477 million and had options to increase its holdings at any time up to the end of 1997.
"The concern is that the purchase price is 22 pesos, versus a stock price that is nearly double that on the open market," said Laura Ehrlich, a food and beverage analyst at Paribas in New York.
Since Anheuser-Busch bought shares from the existing controlling owners of Modelo, however, there will be no dilution on the shares, analysts said.
Other analysts downplayed worries about the price paid and said the stock price may have fallen because the market did not have enough information about the deal.
Despite the short-term jitters in Modelo stock, the deal will probably be positive for Modelo in the long-run as both sides cement a profitable relationship.
Greg Rianhard, an analyst at DA Campbell in Los Angeles, said the move is a clear winner for Anheuser-Busch.
"Anheuser-Busch gets a very immediate bang for their buck and they are increase exposure to what should be one of the fastest growing Latin American markets," he said.
As part of the deal, Anheuser Busch will get 10 of 21 board seats in Modelo -- up from three of 14.
Salomon Brothers said in a report that while Anheuser Busch will have more influence on Modelo, it will not be able to dictate daily operations of the firm.
The deal is also not expected to affect Modelo's distribution in the United States or the distribution of the St-Louis based brewer's products in Mexico, analysts said.
